Quick question: service code 0154 nu sonna enna

சேவை குறியீடு 0154 = ISD (Involving Subdivision / உட்பிரிவு உள்ள பட்டா மாறுதல்).
  • நிலம் பிரிக்கப்படும் பட்டா மாறுதல், எனவே கள ஆய்வும் உட்பிரிவு வரைபடமும் தேவை
  • பணிப்பாய்வு: குடிமகன் / CSC / சார்-பதிவாளர் → SIS (கட்டாய கள ஆய்வு) → மூத்த வரைவாளர் (SD வரைபடம்) → DIS → தாசில்தார் (DSC)
  • கட்டணம்: அரசு ₹400.00 + CSC ₹60.00
  • கால அளவு: 30-35 வேலை நாட்கள்
  • கள ஆய்வு: தேவை

Explain land type / classification codes

The land type code on a parcel controls what verification the SIS must do.
Sample mapping used in the urban extracts:

- 1 — Residential (நடைமுறை குடியிருப்பு)
- 2 — Commercial / mixed use
- 3 — Industrial
- 4 — Agricultural (wet / dry) inside town limits
- 5 — Government poramboke (road, channel, tank, burial ground)
- 6 — Institutional (temple, church, mosque, trust, educational)
- 7 — Vacant / unclassified

Rules that follow:
- A sub-division that changes land type (e.g. agricultural to residential) needs
  reclassification BEFORE the ISD sketch is finalised.
- Poramboke (type 5) cannot be sub-divided or transferred to a private owner
  except through a settlement service code (0179 / 0183) with the sanctioning GO
  quoted.
- Institutional land (type 6) transfer needs the endorsement of the controlling
  authority (HR&CE, Wakf Board, Diocese, or trust) on record.

1. Incomplete Documents
   - Missing required documents (Sale Deed, EC, IDs)
   - Invalid or expired documents
   - Documents not properly attested

   - Area in Sale Deed does not match survey records
   - Sub-division area calculations incorrect
   - Total area of sub-divisions does not equal original survey area

3. Encroachment Issues
   - Encroachment detected during field visit
   - Boundary disputes with neighboring properties
   - Unauthorized construction on land

4. Litigation Flag
   - Ongoing court cases related to the property
   - Disputed ownership claims
   - Stay orders from court

5. Revenue Arrears
   - Pending property taxes
   - Outstanding dues on the survey number
   - Non-payment of water/electricity charges linked to property

6. Invalid Survey Number
   - Survey number does not exist in records

   - Boundary disputes with neighboring properties
   - Unauthorized construction on land

4. Litigation Flag
   - Ongoing court cases related to the property
   - Disputed ownership claims
   - Stay orders from court

5. Revenue Arrears
   - Pending property taxes
   - Outstanding dues on the survey number
   - Non-payment of water/electricity charges linked to property

   - Survey number does not exist in records

What does the SIS guide say about natham and house-site land?

- Natham (habitation) land is recorded in the urban natham chitta with an
  owner name, relative name, relationship code and ownership share.
- Natham settlement is service code 0188; owner name correction in TSLR is 0165.
- A natham parcel with ownership_share blank or "1/1,1" is treated as sole
  ownership; multiple owner rows on one patta_number are joint owners and every
  joint owner must sign at the field visit.
- Door number changes (new_door_number / old_door_number) are handled under
  street and door number modification (service code 0162), not under ISD.

- When a single survey number is partitioned into multiple parcels
- When ownership of part of a survey number is transferred
- When land is sold in parts requiring separate patta
- When inheritance division requires separate land records

Original Survey: 145
First Level Sub-Division: 145/1, 145/2, 145/3
Second Level Sub-Division: 145/1A, 145/1B, 145/2A, 145/2B
Third Level Sub-Division: 145/1A1, 145/1A2, 145/1B1

Sub-Division Numbering Examples:

Example 1: Simple Partition
Survey 145 (1000 sq.m) divided into 2 parts
Result: 145/1 (600 sq.m), 145/2 (400 sq.m)

Example 2: Multiple Sub-Divisions
Survey 267 (2000 sq.m) divided into 4 parts
Result: 267/1 (500 sq.m), 267/2 (500 sq.m), 267/3 (600 sq.m), 267/4 (400 sq.m)

- Ongoing court case related to survey land
- Ownership dispute between multiple parties
- Boundary dispute with neighboring survey
- Stay order from civil or revenue court
- Criminal case involving land fraud or forgery

Types of Litigation:

1. Title Dispute
   - Multiple parties claiming ownership
   - Inherited property dispute
   - Will contest
   - Adverse possession claim

2. Boundary Dispute
   - Disagreement on survey boundaries
   - Conflicting survey documents
   - Encroachment dispute with neighbor

3. Revenue Dispute
   - Property tax assessment dispute
   - Land classification dispute (agricultural vs. residential)
   - Revenue recovery proceedings

4. Criminal Litigation
   - Land grab cases
   - Document forgery
   - Fraudulent sale deed
   - Impersonation

What are the rules for how the submission channel is decided?

Every application carries a submission channel - CSC, citizen or sub_registrar.
It is read off two columns of urban_application_log, and nothing else:

- source_name is "-" (no operator account touched the file): the application
  came in unattended from the Sub-Registrar, where IGRS raised the mutation off
  the registered deed. Channel = sub_registrar.
- source_name holds an operator or VLE code (samples "tut_tct_t131_02",
  "TNEFATUT0540-01") AND camp_flag = "P": the file was keyed in at a special
  revenue camp, where the operator enters it for the citizen standing in front
  of them. The submission is the citizen's own. Channel = citizen.
- source_name holds an operator or VLE code with any other camp_flag (blank,
  "S", "U", "Y"): keyed in at a Common Service Centre counter.
  Channel = CSC.

What does the SIS guide say about land type / classification codes?

The land type code on a parcel controls what verification the SIS must do.
Sample mapping used in the urban extracts:

- 1 — Residential (நடைமுறை குடியிருப்பு)
- 2 — Commercial / mixed use
- 3 — Industrial
- 4 — Agricultural (wet / dry) inside town limits
- 5 — Government poramboke (road, channel, tank, burial ground)
- 6 — Institutional (temple, church, mosque, trust, educational)
- 7 — Vacant / unclassified

Rules that follow:
- A sub-division that changes land type (e.g. agricultural to residential) needs
  reclassification BEFORE the ISD sketch is finalised.
- Poramboke (type 5) cannot be sub-divided or transferred to a private owner
  except through a settlement service code (0179 / 0183) with the sanctioning GO
  quoted.
- Institutional land (type 6) transfer needs the endorsement of the controlling
  authority (HR&CE, Wakf Board, Diocese, or trust) on record.

What are the rules for encroachment: regulatory treatment?

- Private-on-public encroachment (onto road, channel, tank) is reported to the
  local body; the application cannot be approved until the encroached extent is
  removed or regularised by the competent authority.
- Public-on-private and neighbour encroachment is recorded with measured extent
  and a sketch; the transfer may proceed only for the un-encroached extent
  unless the parties settle.
- An encroachment flag set at the field visit is visible to SD and blocks
  automatic approval; resolution typically extends the timeline by 15-30 days.

  • Field visit: required.

- Overdue applications affect officer's performance metrics
- Officers must provide justification for delays beyond 15 days

What are the rules for natham and house-site land?

- Natham (habitation) land is recorded in the urban natham chitta with an
  owner name, relative name, relationship code and ownership share.
- Natham settlement is service code 0188; owner name correction in TSLR is 0165.
- A natham parcel with ownership_share blank or "1/1,1" is treated as sole
  ownership; multiple owner rows on one patta_number are joint owners and every
  joint owner must sign at the field visit.
- Door number changes (new_door_number / old_door_number) are handled under
  street and door number modification (service code 0162), not under ISD.

What is Litigation:
- Ongoing court case related to survey land
- Ownership dispute between multiple parties
- Boundary dispute with neighboring survey
- Stay order from civil or revenue court
- Criminal case involving land fraud or forgery

Types of Litigation:

1. Title Dispute
   - Multiple parties claiming ownership
   - Inherited property dispute
   - Will contest
   - Adverse possession claim

2. Boundary Dispute
   - Disagreement on survey boundaries
   - Conflicting survey documents
   - Encroachment dispute with neighbor

3. Revenue Dispute
   - Property tax assessment dispute
   - Land classification dispute (agricultural vs. residential)
   - Revenue recovery proceedings

4. Criminal Litigation
   - Land grab cases
   - Document forgery
   - Fraudulent sale deed
   - Impersonation

Sub-Division Numbering Examples:

Correct - it did not come from the SRO. SRO is the Sub-Registrar Office, and only its IGRS system issues an IGRS Form 6 number, raised off the registered deed. An application without one was filed at a CSC counter or by the citizen at a revenue camp. For those two channels an empty IGRS field is the rule, not a gap in the record: nothing is missing and there is nothing to chase up with the Sub-Registrar. An IGRS number that IS present is positive evidence the file came from the SRO, and on such a file it is the same number as the application's CAN.

Quick question: What does Sub-Registrar mean?

SRO is the Sub-Registrar Office, where a sale deed is registered. When a deed is registered there, its IGRS system raises the patta mutation off the registered document and issues an IGRS Form 6 number. An application that reaches the SIS desk that way carries that number and no operator code; the officer's own checks on extent and boundaries still apply.

What does the SIS guide say about required documents for isd?

1. Sale Deed
   - Must be registered with Sub-Registrar
   - Original scan copy required
   - Must contain buyer and seller details, survey number, area

2. Encumbrance Certificate (EC)
   - Shows clear title for past 13 years
   - Must be obtained from Sub-Registrar office
   - Valid for 3 months from issue date

3. Survey Sketch
   - Existing survey sketch from revenue records
   - Shows current survey number and boundaries
   - Can be obtained from Tahsildar office

4. Photo ID
   - Aadhaar card (mandatory)
   - Additional ID: Driving License, Voter ID, Passport (any one)
   - Both buyer and seller photo IDs required

5. Photographs
   - Current photographs of the property
   - Boundary stone photographs (if applicable)
   - Minimum 4 photographs from different angles

Explain ownership record: what is held per owner

Ownership of a survey number / sub-division is held as one row per owner, so a
jointly held parcel simply has several owner rows. For each owner the register
keeps: name (English and Tamil), the father's / husband's name with the
relationship (s/o, w/o, d/o), gender, address, the last four digits of the
Aadhaar number, and the ownership share. Two or more owner rows on the same
survey number means the parcel is jointly owned; a single row means a sole
owner.

The register does NOT hold an owner's mobile number, ration card number,
voter ID (EPIC), PIN code, occupation code or door number - those columns are
blank in the source extracts and are not projected. A question about one of
them is answered as "not recorded", not treated as missing data.

What are the rules for sro, the can number, and what an absent igrs number means?

SRO stands for Sub-Registrar Office - the registration office where a sale deed
is registered. Officers say "SRO", "Sub-Registrar" and "sub registrar" for the
same office. When a deed is registered there, the SRO's IGRS system raises the
patta mutation off the registered document and issues an IGRS Form 6 number.
An application that reaches the SIS desk that way carries that number and no
operator code, and its submission channel is sub_registrar.

CAN stands for Citizen Access Number: the unique identity number a citizen is
issued and quotes on an application. most applications carry one.

Which applications carry an IGRS Form 6 number:

- A Sub-Registrar (SRO) referral always carries one. It names the registered
  deed the mutation was raised from, and its value is the same as that
  application's CAN number.
- A CSC application never carries one.

What are the rules for what the sis must not do?

- Do not change a scheduled field visit date without Tahsildar approval.
- Do not approve a sub-division whose extents do not sum to the parent survey.
- Do not transfer poramboke or institutional land without the sanctioning
  authority's order on record.
- Do not proceed past an active court stay.
- Do not accept a sale deed that is not traceable in the Sub-Registrar index.

What does the SIS guide say about ownership record: what is held per owner?

Ownership of a survey number / sub-division is held as one row per owner, so a
jointly held parcel simply has several owner rows. For each owner the register
keeps: name (English and Tamil), the father's / husband's name with the
relationship (s/o, w/o, d/o), gender, address, the last four digits of the
Aadhaar number, and the ownership share. Two or more owner rows on the same
survey number means the parcel is jointly owned; a single row means a sole
owner.

The register does NOT hold an owner's mobile number, ration card number,
voter ID (EPIC), PIN code, occupation code or door number - those columns are
blank in the source extracts and are not projected. A question about one of
them is answered as "not recorded", not treated as missing data.

What are the rules for sale deed, ec and registration linkage?

- The sale deed number in the application (registration_document_number, sample
  form "R/520/1/1188/2022") must match the Sub-Registrar's registered index and
  the registration_place (e.g. "Tuticorin Joint I", "Tuticorin Joint II").
- IGRS Form 6 number is a 12-digit reference (sample "Not recorded") linking the
  registered document to the mutation request. It appears on
  urban_application_log, the NISD/ISD application-info rows and the IGRS owner
  row.
- Encumbrance Certificate must show a clear title for the preceding 13 years and
  be within 3 months of its issue date at the time of verification.
- igrs_auto_mutation_flag = Y means mutation is expected to post automatically
  after registration; the SIS still verifies extent and boundaries before the
  patta transfer order is generated.
- transaction_status on the transfer detail: "01" = transfer effected,
...

What is a CAN number, and does its length tell me the submission channel?

CAN is the Citizen Access Number, the unique identity number a citizen quotes on an application; most applications carry one. Its length names the counter that ISSUED it, not the channel the application came in through - 15 digits (133 series) from a CSC counter, 12 digits from the TN citizen portal. A Sub-Registrar referral carries a 12-digit portal-issued CAN even though no citizen keyed it in, so a 12-digit CAN does not mean "citizen" and a 15-digit CAN does not mean "CSC". The channel is decided by the source name and camp flag on the file.

What does the SIS guide say about minimum extent and sub-division limits?

- Minimum measurable urban parcel: 1 sq.m; areas recorded to 2 decimal places
  in square metres. Extent may also be shown in ares (1 are = 100 sq.m).
- Sample minimum plot for a residential sub-division inside a corporation:
  300 sq.ft (~27.87 sq.m) frontage-permitting; local body building rules
  override where stricter.
- A sub-division that would leave any resulting parcel below the local minimum
  is refused; the applicant is asked to revise the partition.
- Maximum sub-division depth: 3 levels (145 -> 145/1 -> 145/1A -> 145/1A1).
  Beyond this the officer records a remark and refers to DIS.
- Sum of all sub-division extents MUST equal the parent survey extent within a
  tolerance of +/- 0.5%. Anything outside tolerance needs re-survey and a DIS
  variance note.

What are the rules for land type / classification codes?

The land type code on a parcel controls what verification the SIS must do.
Sample mapping used in the urban extracts:

- 1 — Residential (நடைமுறை குடியிருப்பு)
- 2 — Commercial / mixed use
- 3 — Industrial
- 4 — Agricultural (wet / dry) inside town limits
- 5 — Government poramboke (road, channel, tank, burial ground)
- 6 — Institutional (temple, church, mosque, trust, educational)
- 7 — Vacant / unclassified

Rules that follow:
- A sub-division that changes land type (e.g. agricultural to residential) needs
  reclassification BEFORE the ISD sketch is finalised.
- Poramboke (type 5) cannot be sub-divided or transferred to a private owner
  except through a settlement service code (0179 / 0183) with the sanctioning GO
  quoted.
- Institutional land (type 6) transfer needs the endorsement of the controlling
  authority (HR&CE, Wakf Board, Diocese, or trust) on record.

You are the SIS AI Assistant for Tamil Nadu Sub Inspector Surveyor officers. Answer only from the department's register; never invent an application number, count, or date.
What does the SIS guide say about sro, the can number, and what an absent igrs number means?

SRO stands for Sub-Registrar Office - the registration office where a sale deed
is registered. Officers say "SRO", "Sub-Registrar" and "sub registrar" for the
same office. When a deed is registered there, the SRO's IGRS system raises the
patta mutation off the registered document and issues an IGRS Form 6 number.
An application that reaches the SIS desk that way carries that number and no
operator code, and its submission channel is sub_registrar.

CAN stands for Citizen Access Number: the unique identity number a citizen is
issued and quotes on an application. most applications carry one.

Which applications carry an IGRS Form 6 number:

- A Sub-Registrar (SRO) referral always carries one. It names the registered
  deed the mutation was raised from, and its value is the same as that
  application's CAN number.
- A CSC application never carries one.

  automatic approval; resolution typically extends the timeline by 15-30 days.

What does the temporary number format mean?

The format is {existing_subdivision}/T{sequence}. The part before /T is the existing subdivision being split (0 if the survey has no prior subdivision). T stands for Temporary. The number after T is a sequence counter. For example, 3/T1 means "first temporary parcel from existing subdivision 3", and 0/T2 means "second temporary parcel from a survey with no prior subdivision".

- Overdue applications are flagged in officer's dashboard with red indicator
- Officers receive escalation notifications for overdue applications
- Overdue applications affect officer's performance metrics
- Officers must provide justification for delays beyond 15 days

- Private-on-public encroachment (onto road, channel, tank) is reported to the
  local body; the application cannot be approved until the encroached extent is
  removed or regularised by the competent authority.
- Public-on-private and neighbour encroachment is recorded with measured extent
  and a sketch; the transfer may proceed only for the un-encroached extent
  unless the parties settle.
- An encroachment flag set at the field visit is visible to SD and blocks
  automatic approval; resolution typically extends the timeline by 15-30 days.

When a deed is registered there, its IGRS system raises the patta mutation off the registered document and issues an IGRS Form 6 number.   variance note.

What are the rules for required documents for isd?

1. Sale Deed
   - Must be registered with Sub-Registrar
   - Original scan copy required
   - Must contain buyer and seller details, survey number, area

2. Encumbrance Certificate (EC)
   - Shows clear title for past 13 years
   - Must be obtained from Sub-Registrar office
   - Valid for 3 months from issue date

3. Survey Sketch
   - Existing survey sketch from revenue records
   - Shows current survey number and boundaries
   - Can be obtained from Tahsildar office

4. Photo ID
   - Aadhaar card (mandatory)
   - Additional ID: Driving License, Voter ID, Passport (any one)
   - Both buyer and seller photo IDs required

5. Photographs
   - Current photographs of the property
   - Boundary stone photographs (if applicable)
   - Minimum 4 photographs from different angles

You are the SIS AI Assistant for Tamil Nadu Sub Inspector Surveyor officers. Answer only from the department's register; never invent an application number, count, or date.
Explain how the submission channel is decided

Every application carries a submission channel - CSC, citizen or sub_registrar.
It is read off two columns of urban_application_log, and nothing else:

- source_name is "-" (no operator account touched the file): the application
  came in unattended from the Sub-Registrar, where IGRS raised the mutation off
  the registered deed. Channel = sub_registrar.
- source_name holds an operator or VLE code (samples "tut_tct_t131_02",
  "TNEFATUT0540-01") AND camp_flag = "P": the file was keyed in at a special
  revenue camp, where the operator enters it for the citizen standing in front
  of them. The submission is the citizen's own. Channel = citizen.
- source_name holds an operator or VLE code with any other camp_flag (blank,
  "S", "U", "Y"): keyed in at a Common Service Centre counter.
  Channel = CSC.

  • SLA: 30-35 working days.
  • Field visit: required.

Explain sro, the can number, and what an absent igrs number means

SRO stands for Sub-Registrar Office - the registration office where a sale deed
is registered. Officers say "SRO", "Sub-Registrar" and "sub registrar" for the
same office. When a deed is registered there, the SRO's IGRS system raises the
patta mutation off the registered document and issues an IGRS Form 6 number.
An application that reaches the SIS desk that way carries that number and no
operator code, and its submission channel is sub_registrar.

CAN stands for Citizen Access Number: the unique identity number a citizen is
issued and quotes on an application. most applications carry one.

Which applications carry an IGRS Form 6 number:

- A Sub-Registrar (SRO) referral always carries one. It names the registered
  deed the mutation was raised from, and its value is the same as that
  application's CAN number.
- A CSC application never carries one.

What are the rules for required documents for nisd?

1. Sale Deed
   - Registered with Sub-Registrar
   - Original scan copy required
   - Must match survey number in application

2. Encumbrance Certificate (EC)
   - Clear title for past 13 years
   - Valid for 3 months from issue date

3. Photo ID
   - Aadhaar card of buyer and seller
   - Additional ID proof (any one government ID)

4. Patta Copy
   - Current patta copy showing previous owner
   - Can be obtained from Tahsildar office or online portal
You are the SIS AI Assistant for Tamil Nadu Sub Inspector Surveyor officers. Answer only from the department's register; never invent an application number, count, or date.
What are the rules for ownership record: what is held per owner?

Ownership of a survey number / sub-division is held as one row per owner, so a
jointly held parcel simply has several owner rows. For each owner the register
keeps: name (English and Tamil), the father's / husband's name with the
relationship (s/o, w/o, d/o), gender, address, the last four digits of the
Aadhaar number, and the ownership share. Two or more owner rows on the same
survey number means the parcel is jointly owned; a single row means a sole
owner.

The register does NOT hold an owner's mobile number, ration card number,
voter ID (EPIC), PIN code, occupation code or door number - those columns are
blank in the source extracts and are not projected. A question about one of
them is answered as "not recorded", not treated as missing data.

  owner name, relative name, relationship code and ownership share.

  joint owner must sign at the field visit.
- Door number changes (new_door_number / old_door_number) are handled under
  street and door number modification (service code 0162), not under ISD.

1. Sale Deed

   - Original scan copy required

2. Encumbrance Certificate (EC)
   - Shows clear title for past 13 years
   - Must be obtained from Sub-Registrar office
   - Valid for 3 months from issue date

3. Survey Sketch
   - Existing survey sketch from revenue records
   - Shows current survey number and boundaries
   - Can be obtained from Tahsildar office

4. Photo ID
   - Aadhaar card (mandatory)
   - Additional ID: Driving License, Voter ID, Passport (any one)
   - Both buyer and seller photo IDs required

5. Photographs
   - Current photographs of the property
   - Boundary stone photographs (if applicable)
   - Minimum 4 photographs from different angles

SRO is the Sub-Registrar Office, where a sale deed is registered. When a deed is registered there, its IGRS system raises the patta mutation off the registered document and issues an IGRS Form 6 number.   be within 3 months of its issue date at the time of verification.

  after registration; the SIS still verifies extent and boundaries before the
  patta transfer order is generated.

  in square metres. Extent may also be shown in ares (1 are = 100 sq.m).

- Maximum sub-division depth: 3 levels (145 -> 145/1 -> 145/1A -> 145/1A1).
  Beyond this the officer records a remark and refers to DIS.
- Sum of all sub-division extents MUST equal the parent survey extent within a
  tolerance of +/- 0.5%. Anything outside tolerance needs re-survey and a DIS
  variance note.

What does the SIS guide say about how the submission channel is decided?

Every application carries a submission channel - CSC, citizen or sub_registrar.
It is read off two columns of urban_application_log, and nothing else:

- source_name is "-" (no operator account touched the file): the application
  came in unattended from the Sub-Registrar, where IGRS raised the mutation off
  the registered deed. Channel = sub_registrar.
- source_name holds an operator or VLE code (samples "tut_tct_t131_02",
  "TNEFATUT0540-01") AND camp_flag = "P": the file was keyed in at a special
  revenue camp, where the operator enters it for the citizen standing in front
  of them. The submission is the citizen's own. Channel = citizen.
- source_name holds an operator or VLE code with any other camp_flag (blank,
  "S", "U", "Y"): keyed in at a Common Service Centre counter.
  Channel = CSC.

How do temporary numbers become final subdivision numbers?

Typically, the first parcel (T1) retains the existing subdivision number, and subsequent parcels (T2, T3, etc.) receive new sequential numbers. For example, 3/T1 becomes 3 and 3/T2 becomes 4.    - Property tax assessment dispute
   - Land classification dispute (agricultural vs. residential)
